data.title: Equinor ASA: Announcement of cash dividend of NOK 3.7448 per share for second quarter 2026
data.description:
Equinor ASA (OSE: EQNR, NYSE: EQNR) announced on 22 July 2026 a cash dividend per share of USD 0.39 for second quarter 2026.

The NOK cash dividend per share is based on average USDNOK fixing rate from Norges Bank in the period plus/minus three business days from record date 16 November 2026, in total seven business days. Average Norges Bank fixing rate for this period was 9.6021. Total cash dividend for second quarter 2026 is consequently NOK 3.7448 per share.

On 25 November 2026, the cash dividend will be paid to relevant shareholders on Oslo Børs (Oslo Stock Exchange) and to holders of American Depositary Receipts ("ADRs") on the New York Stock Exchange.

This information is published in accordance with the requirements of the Continuing Obligations and is subject to the disclosure requirements pursuant to section 5-12 of the Norwegian Securities Trading Act.

data.title: Webuild Now Holds Over 60% Stake in Trevi
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Italian construction and civil engineering company Webuild said late Thursday that it now holds 60.82% of the shares in Trevi-Finanziaria Industriale through share purchases and offer acceptances.

Webuild earlier this week received clearance for the takeover from the Italian Competition Authority. The regulator decided not to open an inquiry as it doesn't significantly impede effective competition in the markets concerned and doesn't entail the creation or strengthening of a dominant position, Webuild said.

Webuild made an initial bid of 4.50 euros per share for Trevi in July, before later agreeing to pay 5.165 euros a share, or around 339 million euros ($371.8 million).

In a statement Thursday, Webuild Chief Executive Pietro Salini said that the deal has now effectively come to fruition and "allows the group to unlock significant synergies, strengthening the competitiveness of the entire supply chain across Italy's industrial system."

The offer, which is mandatory and not subject to any conditions, closes Friday.

data.title: Anthropic's Australian data centre overwhelmingly opposed by residents
data.description:
Key points:
  • Project draws 595 objections or delay requests from nearly 600 public submissions, filing shows
  • Data centre's planned computing load reaches 1.44 gigawatts, among Australia's biggest
  • Most objections cite water, power, noise, road damage and housing concerns

By Byron Kaye

A data centre planned in regional Australia with Anthropic as its anchor tenant is overwhelmingly opposed by residents, a filing for the project showed, setting the scene for a showdown between the AI company and the community hosting its first Australian facility.

Of nearly 600 public submissions on the proposed Western Downs Digital Park, about 250 km (155 miles) west of Brisbane, two expressed support for the project and one was neutral, according to the filing. The remaining 595 opposed it or asked for a delay until developers cleared certain environmental hurdles, the filing said.

"A significant number of submissions raise reasonable matters regarding water, power, noise, roads, housing and the scale of the project," the filing, lodged on behalf of developer Zerra DC, said.

A Zerra spokesperson said the project took seriously the submissions, which "reinforce that people want a greater say in how the project develops". The developer was expanding its community engagement and planned to report changes demanded by the public.

Anthropic declined to comment.

The initial response, though far from binding, gives a sense of the souring relationship between communities and the so-called AI factories being built at pace around the world in a boom McKinsey has valued at $7 trillion by 2030.

Already in Australia, Goodman Group scrapped a roughly A$1.2 billion data centre planned for Sydney in September after a public backlash, while NextDC delayed a project in Melbourne amid resident concerns about energy use, triggering a shares selldown.

The Anthropic project is on farmland and further from the suburbs, but with a planned computing load of 1.44 gigawatts would be one of the country's biggest. About one-third of the submissions were from people who lived within 200 km of the site, the filing said.

Objectors mostly cited concerns about water use, electricity demand and prices, noise, road damage from construction traffic and pressure on housing.

Before the data centre project named Anthropic as its tenant on September 15, it had received five objections in a month, a log of public comments showed, with the rest arriving between then and November 11, when the local government stopped accepting submissions.

The filing about Australian data centre submissions was published the same week Anthropic made its stock market debut on Wall St, pricing its initial public offering on November 18 in a deal that valued the company at around $1.5 trillion.

data.title: Turkey's Kiler Holding rejects lawmaker's share transaction allegations, files criminal complaint
data.description:
Kiler Holding , a Turkish conglomerate, has rejected a lawmaker's allegations concerning share transactions involving the company and its shareholders, saying it had filed a criminal complaint against him and lawsuits seeking damages.

Umit Ozlale, a member of the opposition New Party, questioned a series of share sales, purchases and transfers involving Kiler shareholders and a fund in comments at a press conference in parliament and in a post on X. He also asked whether Turkey's Capital Markets Board, or SPK, had reviewed the transactions.

Ozlale has been a leading figure among those in parliament trying to scrutinise Turkey’s recent investment funds crisis.

Kiler Holding, which is active in sectors including construction and energy, said in a statement on Thursday evening that the allegations were unfounded and that the company and its shareholders were being targeted for political reasons.

The company said all the transactions complied with relevant regulations and that the required disclosures had been made through the public disclosure platform KAP.

Records relating to the transactions were transparent and available for independent audit and examination by the relevant authorities, it said.

data.title: SpaceX sells $32B in AI chip debt above 8% yield: report
data.description:
Key points:
  • SpaceX sold $32B of bonds to fund its purchase of artificial intelligence chips on Thursday, in a complicated and relatively high-yielding transaction that may serve as a model for a wave of similar financings to come, according to a Bloomberg report.
  • The debt offering was designed to keep the borrowing off SpaceX’s balance sheet and is part of a more than $40B financing that also includes bank loans.
  • The deal will effectively allow SpaceX to buy Nvidia Corp. chips that the rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company will lease for about five years.
  • The debt was sold on Thursday in three parts, the report said. Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Apollo Global Management Inc ran the transaction.
  • The biggest of the three portions sold on Thursday, about $25.2B of Class A3 notes, was priced at a yield of 8.259%, a relatively high level for an investment-grade security. The average US high-grade note yielded 5.95% on Thursday, according to Bloomberg index data. The bonds also offered a premium over SpaceX’s existing debt from its June offering, which tanked in the secondary market after the securities started trading.

data.title: SpiceJet faces over 7,600 passenger complaints amid widespread flight cancellations
data.description:
The Centre has received over 7,000 complaints against beleaguered SpiceJet on its passenger complaints redressal portal, AirSewa, amid continued flight cancellations as well as passenger inconvenience.

According to the Ministry of Civil Aviation’s grievance page, 7,674 grievances were listed against the airline in data dated November 19.

SpiceJet cancellations raise winter travel concerns

Sources said most of the airline’s scheduled flights were cancelled on Friday, and its services did not appear in booking results on most online travel portals. The airline is currently operating around 10 aircraft, comprising aircraft from its own fleet and wet-leased planes.

These disruptions come ahead of the peak winter travel period, raising concerns about passenger inconvenience, alternative flight availability, and replacement fares.

However, the wider impact on domestic passenger traffic and fares is likely to be limited, given that SpiceJet’s market share stood at only 0.6 per cent in September, down from 1.2 per cent in August, according to Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) data.

Nevertheless, passengers booked on cancelled services could face higher last-minute fares, particularly on routes with limited alternatives.

The impact on fares would depend on seat availability on competing airlines on the affected routes during the winter travel period.

DGCA flags repeated regulatory violations

Meanwhile, the DGCA has issued a show-cause notice dated November 17, giving SpiceJet seven days to respond to alleged regulatory and operational non-compliance.

The notice flagged several repeated regulatory violations.

Furthermore, the regulator observed that a majority of SpiceJet’s fleet remained grounded and that the airline had failed to submit a credible plan to bring these aircraft back into service.

SpiceJet seeks ₹5,500 crore to revive operations

The regulatory scrutiny comes as the cash-strapped airline seeks fresh funding to strengthen its financial position, rebuild capacity and support its revival.

On Wednesday, SpiceJet’s board approved a proposal to raise ₹5,500 crore, subject to the necessary shareholder and regulatory approvals.

The airline has been struggling to pay employee salaries for several months amid a cash crunch.

Moreover, the budget carrier faces legal hurdles, including insolvency petitions filed by lessors and payment claims involving former promoter Kalanithi Maran and KAL Airways.

data.title: India Cements to initiate recovery of ₹26 crore arbitration award from Zuari, after SC dismisses SLP
data.description:
India Cements Ltd informed exchanges that the Supreme Court on Wednesday dismissed a Special Leave Petition (SLP) filed by Zuari Cement against India Cements in a dispute arising from a 2002 marketing agreement.

This has now cleared the way for India Cements to initiate recovery proceedings for ₹26.40 crore along with applicable interest, the company said.

As per the filing, the dispute relates to an Agreement in May 2002 between India Cements and Sri Vishnu Cement (which was subsequently merged with Zuari Cement).

While the Arbitral Tribunal had passed an award in favour of India Cements, directing Sri Vishnu Cement to pay ₹26.40 crore along with applicable interest, Zuari Cement had then challenged the award before the Madras High Court, where Zuari obtained a favourable judgement for itself.

India Cements then appealed to the High Court and managed to get it set aside, following which Zuari had filed an SLP before the Supreme Court.

“The company shall now initiate appropriate proceedings for recovery of the awarded amount, together with applicable interest, from Zuari Cements,” India Cements said in the filing.

Shares of India Cements were trading at ₹324.50, up 1 per cent on the BSE, at the time of filing the report.
